extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and supervisory examiners); patent practitioners may also consult
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for treating Requests for Continued Examination (RCEs) under 37 CFR 1.114 and for preparing Office actions under 37 CFR 1.104, including eligibility, what constitutes a proper/improper RCE, effects on appeals, citation and rejection practices, and required form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114, the application must be a utility or plant application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995. The RCE must be filed on or after May 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This eligibility test is repeatedly required in determining whether to treat a filing as an RCE and which form paragraphs to use. If the application does not meet these filing-date/type criteria, use Form PTO-2051 (Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (RCE)).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE must include required fee and a submission (37 CFR 1.17(e) and 1.114)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for continued examination must be accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) and a submission as required by 37 CFR 1.114 (e.g., IDS, amendment to written description/claims/drawings, new arguments, or new evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If either the fee or the submission is missing, the RCE is improper. If the fee is missing but a submission is present, note whether the submission has been entered (generally it should not be entered unless it obviously places the application in condition for allowance with SPE approval).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper RCE: responsiveness to last outstanding Office action (37 CFR 1.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE accompanied by the fee and a submission that includes a reply which is responsive within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.111 to the last outstanding Office action will result in withdrawal of the finality of the last Office action and entry and consideration of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submission is not fully responsive but is a bona fide attempt to reply, notify applicant that the submission is not fully responsive, explain why, and give a new time period to complete the reply (use form paragraph 7.42.08).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE: treatment and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: If the RCE lacks the fee and/or the required submission, or the submission is not a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply (e.g., an IDS only), the request is an improper RCE and should be treated accordingly (appeal may still be withdrawn; time periods not tolled).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When improper, the Office will generally not enter the submission. Use the designated form paragraphs (e.g., 7.42.16 or PTO-2051) to notify applicant. Exception: an amendment that obviously places the application in condition for allowance may be entered with SPE approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after allowance or Quayle action reopens prosecution if eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for continued examination filed after allowance or after an Office action under Ex parte Quayle, when eligible and the fee is timely paid, reopens prosecution pursuant to 37 CFR 1.114 and the applicant’s submission will be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the RCE was filed after the issue fee was paid, a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 to withdraw the application from issue must have been filed and granted. Use form paragraph 7.42.05 to notify applicant that prosecution has been reopened.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after Notice of Appeal but before Board decision withdraws appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files an RCE after filing a Notice of Appeal to the Board but prior to a decision on the appeal, the RCE will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and to reopen prosecution before the examiner, regardless of whether the RCE is proper or improper (see 37 CFR 1.114(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will withdraw the appeal upon filing of an RCE. Applicants should advise the Board when an RCE is filed in an application containing an appeal awaiting decision; otherwise the Board may refuse to vacate a decision rendered after the filing of the RCE but before Office recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of appeal withdrawal: allowed vs. no allowed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon withdrawal of the appeal, if no claim is allowed the application is abandoned; if at least one claim is allowed, the application should be passed to issue on the allowed claim(s). Claims allowable only by dependency on rejected claims are treated as if rejected and canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is at least one allowed claim but formal matters are outstanding, applicant should be given a shortened statutory period of one month or thirty days (whichever is longer) to correct formal matters. Use form paragraphs 7.42.10–7.42.14 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE after Board decision but before further appeal/civil action — res judicata and 'law of the case'
rubrics_metrics.description: A Board decision is res judicata and the 'law of the case' and thus controlling in that application and related applications; a submission containing arguments without amendment of the rejected claims or submission of a showing of facts will not be effective to remove such rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An RCE filed after a Board decision but before filing notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencement of civil action will withdraw the appeal and reopen prosecution only if timely (generally within the two-month time for seeking court review) and accompanied by fee and submission. Use form paragraph 7.42.07 to notify applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE after Board decision but missing fee/submission — examiner actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE is filed after a Board decision but before further appeal/civil action and lacks the fee or submission, the examiner should notify applicant that the RCE is improper (use form paragraph 7.42.16) and, depending on timing, include the paragraph with a Notice of Allowability or Notice of Abandonment or on PTOL-90.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission accompanies an improper RCE, generally do not enter it; include a statement whether the submission has been entered. If application is not the eligible filing type/dates, use PTO-2051 instead of 7.42.16.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE not available after filing of notice of appeal to Federal Circuit or commencement of civil action (unless terminated)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.114 is not available in an application after filing of a Notice of Appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencement of a civil action in district court unless the appeal/civil action is terminated and the application is still pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an RCE is filed after court review, examiner should bring the application to SPE or special program examiner to determine propriety. Unless application contains allowed claims (or court mandate indicates Office action), termination of unsuccessful court review results in abandonment. See MPEP § 1216.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form usage: PTO/SB/30 and PTO-2051
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/30 'Request for Continued Examination (RCE) Transmittal' may be used by applicant for filing an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114. Form PTO-2051 'Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (RCE)' is used by Technology Centers to notify applicant that continued examination does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate form paragraph shown in MPEP (e.g., 7.42.05–7.42.16) depending on the RCE timing, contents, and eligibility. Do not use form paragraph 7.42.16 if the application is not of eligible filing date/type—use PTO-2051 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's duty to make a thorough study and prior art investigation (37 CFR 1.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: On taking up an application, the examiner shall make a thorough study of it and a thorough investigation of the available prior art relating to the subject matter of the claimed invention; examination shall be complete with respect to statutory compliance and patentability (and matters of form unless otherwise indicated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination should be complete as to all matters, except in appropriate circumstances (misjoinder, fundamental defects) where action may be limited. Matters of form need not be raised until a claim is found allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: When rejecting claims for novelty/obviousness, cite best references and explain pertinence
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims for want of novelty or obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references available. When a reference is complex or shows other inventions, designate the particular part relied on as nearly as practicable and clearly explain the pertinence of each reference and specify each rejected claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103, set out how a reference is modified or how plural references are combined. Include particular figures/pages/paragraphs when necessary to provide adequate information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may rely on applicant admissions and facts within examiner's knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims, the examiner may rely upon admissions by the applicant (or patent owner in reexamination) and, for applications, may rely upon facts within the examiner's knowledge pursuant to 37 CFR 1.104(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a rejection is based on facts within an Office employee's personal knowledge, the data shall be as specific as possible and, when called for by the applicant, supported by an affidavit of such employee, subject to contradiction/explanation by applicant affidavits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 102(e)/(f)/(g) subject matter as prior art and joint research agreement exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter developed by another person that qualifies as prior art only under 35 U.S.C. 102(e), (f) or (g) may be used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103 unless the entire rights were commonly owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment at the time the claimed invention was made; joint research agreement conditions can establish common ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To overcome a 103 rejection based on such prior art via 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(2), the applicant must provide a statement that the prior art and claimed invention were made by parties to a joint research agreement in effect on or before the date of invention and that the claimed invention resulted from activities within the scope of that agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims precluded by waiver in published statutory invention registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in an original application naming an inventor will be rejected as precluded by a waiver in a published statutory invention registration naming that inventor if the same subject matter is claimed in the application and the statutory invention registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar rule applies to reissue applications when the reissue seeks subject matter waived in the statutory invention registration and not previously covered by issued claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation particulars required when citing references
rubrics_metrics.description: When domestic patents are cited, state numbers, dates, and names of patentees; when domestic patent application publications are cited, state publication number, date, and applicant names; when foreign published applications or patents are cited, state country, numbers, dates, and names and identify particular pages/sheets if only part is involved; printed publications require author, title, date, pages/plates, and place of publication or where a copy can be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient data to enable applicant or patent owner to identify the documents. Attach Notice of References Cited (PTO-892) to applicant copies of the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance must be documented and may be communicated
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes the record does not make clear reasons for allowing claims, the examiner may set forth such reasoning, incorporate it into an Office action rejecting other claims or communicate it separately to applicant. Applicant may file a statement commenting on the reasons for allowance within a specified time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure by the examiner to respond to any statement commenting on reasons for allowance does not give rise to any implication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action composition and required information on replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Office Action Summary Form PTOL-326 should be used as the first page of Office actions; it signifies certain information including the period set for reply, any attachments, and a 'Summary of Action' indicating the position on all claims and identifying allowed claims. Attachments share paper number and are part of the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies to Office actions should include the application number, 4-digit art unit number, and the examiner's name to expedite handling. Applicants are encouraged to include the 4-digit confirmation number on every paper filed. Conclude actions with one of form paragraphs 7.100, 7.101, or 7.102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone inquiry/contact procedures and related form paragraph content
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.100–7.102 provide standard closing/contact language — include name and telephone number of examiner, normal duty hours, supervisor contact if examiner unreachable, and PAIR/Private PAIR access information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inserts: bracket 1 - examiner name; bracket 2 - phone number; bracket 3 - work days; brackets 4/5 - duty hours; bracket 6 - SPE name; bracket 7 - SPE phone number. Provide PAIR portal info and EBC contact for Private PAIR access questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone discussions and examiner's amendment practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner may indicate that a discussion with applicant's representative may result in agreements to place the application in condition for allowance and may telephone the representative within about two weeks. Resulting amendments may be made by the applicant's attorney/agent or by the examiner in an examiner's amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When extensive amendments are necessary, it is preferable they be filed by the attorney/agent to reduce Office workload and provide a better file wrapper record, including applicant's arguments for allowability as required by 37 CFR 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional explanation needed in exceptional or pro se cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In exceptional cases or pro se cases where the inventor is unfamiliar with patent law and practice, a more complete explanation in the Office action may be needed to satisfy the requirements of 37 CFR 1.104(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include particular figures, pages, paragraphs of references, and any relevant comments briefly stated when necessary to provide adequate information.
